title: António Manuel Ne Vunda's embassy from Kongo to Rome, 1604–1608
summary: King Álvaro II of Kongo sent Ne Vunda to Pope Paul V in 1604. He went by way of Brazil and Spain, took more than three years, reached Rome on 3 January 1608, and died two days later. He was the first African ambassador to the Holy See, and a painting of him hangs in the Quirinal beside the Japanese Keichō embassy's. The source names the countries and no ports: the crossing is drawn from the Congo coast to Brazil and on to Spain, the road to Rome straight.
